Mark the student's response to a question from the 2024 NSW HSC Ancient History exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting. The images attached before this text are the sources the question refers to, in letter order; read them and judge how well the response uses them. Judge the response the way HSC Ancient History markers do: a direct answer to the question, a sustained judgement where the directive verb asks for one, specific and accurate evidence (dates, names, cases, legislation, sources, historians) and the terms of the course. Do not reward length or narrative for its own sake.

Question 3 [7 marks]: Which culture had more influence in Pompeii and Herculaneum: Greek or Egyptian? Support your response using evidence from Sources B and C and other relevant sources.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 7):
6–7 marks: Provides an informed judgement about whether Greek or Egyptian culture had more influence in Pompeii and Herculaneum | Supports the response using evidence from Sources B and C and refers to other relevant source(s) | Communicates ideas and information using appropriate historical terms and concepts
4–5 marks: Provides a judgement about the influence of Greek and/or Egyptian culture in Pompeii and Herculaneum | Supports the response with reference to Sources B and C and other relevant source(s) | Communicates using some historical terms and concepts
2–3 marks: Provides some relevant information about Greek and/or Egyptian culture in Pompeii and/or Herculaneum | May refer to Sources B and/or C and/or other sources | May use some historical terms and/or concepts
1 marks: Makes a general statement(s) about Greek and/or Egyptian culture in Pompeii or Herculaneum


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
Possible judgements
• Greek culture was more influential, as denoted by the original Greek settlement of the towns, and shown through art, architecture, religion
• Egyptian culture was very influential, with the Cult of Isis and fascination with Egyptian exoticism evident throughout both towns.
Source B
• Source B is a fresco from Herculaneum depicting Hercules, the patron god of the town
• These are Greek gods which were adopted by the early Greek settlers in the area, and who were still celebrated and worshipped at the time of the town’s destruction, showing their importance.
Source C
• Source C is from Mary Beard and talks about a statue of Isis, the goddess of the Egyptian cult, showing its influence in Pompeii
• However, Beard refers to the Egyptian statue as appearing to have been influenced by Greek imagery, ‘she hardly appears Egyptian at all’.
Other sources
• Egypt: Nile mosaic, Temple of Isis, statuettes found in lararia, Anubis mosaic
• Greece: Architecture eg Odeon Theatre, Augustales with Greek frescoes, Alexander mosaic.
